analysis:
Documentation-only batch. CHANGELOG.md head lines 4531-5371 are unchanged historical entries; the changed range is head lines 11-39, where a v0.10.10 candidate section describes the new `darkbloom waitlist` command and approval gating for new sandbox setups and new cluster pairs. That section is visible only in the file_changes excerpt, not in the units. changelog.d/feature-waitlists.md is removed (base lines 1-7) because its content was folded into CHANGELOG. docs/operations/provider-release.md is a metadata-only unit; the excerpt shows a version-note rewrite from 0.10.9 to 0.10.10.

No source code is in this batch, so no security regression can be cited. Integration should check the waitlist feature itself in the provider CLI/source batches against TB-013/T-061 (sandbox setup runs the downloaded installer as the Mac owner) and TB-014/T-062 (cluster GPU limit). Specifically: (1) waitlist approval is a coordinator response; it gates feature onboarding and must not be treated as an authorization or security control. (2) The documented fallback 'a coordinator without waitlists lets setup go on as before' is a fail-open path. A network attacker or malicious coordinator response could skip the gate. That only bypasses onboarding policy, not installer integrity checks, so it matters only if the gate is relied on for security. (3) Joining a waitlist is documented as sending only account data, nothing about the Mac; this should be verified against A-008 token use and data exposure. (4) Existing paired or installed setups skip the gate, so the persisted-state check must not be spoofable in any way that matters for security. (5) The `--json` output prints the coordinator's answer; confirm it contains no tokens.

T-041 and other cache entries in the historical changelog are unchanged.
